subject: Using generated quantities to calculate log likelihood

messages.author: e671f21ee99dc4ee
messages.subject: Using generated quantities to calculate log likelihood
parts:
Hi all,

I just started to use stan to run a hierarchical model to explain a ecological data set. Briefly, I'd like to see if the phytoplankton (algae) density is related to the diversity of zooplankton (grazers) in ~1000 lakes and how does this relationship differ among different ecoregion as well as the % of omnivore zooplankton in the lake. I can provide more information if needed. 

I wrote a stan script (please see the "My working stan script" below) and it works fine (I tested it with only 500 iterations). However, if I add a generated quantities block as bellow, then it reports to me that one of the variable (mu_phyD) is not found. This variable is already defined in the model block. 

Two questions here:
1. Should I define the mu_phyD variable in other block, so that log likelihood can be calculated?
2. I tried to vectorize my model but couldn't figure out how. Would someone give me a hint?

Thank you for your help!


The generated quantities block:

generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  for (n in 1:N){
    log_lik[n] = normal_lpdf( phyDenL[n] | mu_phyD[n], sigma_phyDen);
  }
}

My working stan script:

data {
  int<lower=1> N; // the number of observations
  int<lower=1> J; // the number of Omernik level 3 ecoregion
  int<lower=1,upper=J> region[N];
  int<lower=1> K1; // number of column of the model matrix (6 because zpSR is not included)
  matrix[N, K1] mod5; // N (# of obs) by K (# of predictors) model matrix 
  vector[N] phyDenL; // response variable, Y
  
  vector[N] zpSR; // 
  int<lower=1> K2; // number of column of the model matrix determining the effects of zpSR
  matrix[N, K2] mod5_1; // the model matrix determining the effects of zpSR
}
parameters {
  vector[K1] gamma;
  vector<lower=0>[K1] tau;
  vector[K1] beta_raw[J]; //Applying Matt's trick
  
  vector[K2] gamma_beta_zpSR;
  vector<lower=0>[K2] tau_beta_zpSR;
  vector[K2] b_raw[J]; //Applying Matt's trick
  
  real<lower=0> sigma_phyDen; //standard deviation of the individual observations
}
transformed parameters{
  vector[K1] beta[J];
  vector[K2] b[J];
  for(j in 1:J){
    beta[j] = gamma + tau .* beta_raw[j];
    b[j] = gamma_beta_zpSR + tau_beta_zpSR .* b_raw[j];
  }
}
model {
  vector[N] mu_phyD;
  vector[N] beta_zpSR;
  
  //priors
  gamma ~ normal(0,5); //weakly informative priors on the regression coefficients
  tau ~ cauchy(0,2.5); //weakly informative priors
  gamma_beta_zpSR ~ normal(0,5); //weakly informative priors on the regression coefficients
  tau_beta_zpSR ~ cauchy(0,2.5); //weakly informative priors
  sigma_phyDen ~ gamma(2,0.1); //weakly informative priors
  
  //likelihood
  for (j in 1:J){
    b_raw[j]~normal(0, 1);
    beta_raw[j]~normal(0, 1);
  }
  
  for (i in 1:N){
    beta_zpSR[i] = mod5_1[i]*b[region[i]];
    mu_phyD[i] = mod5[i]*beta[region[i]] + zpSR[i]*beta_zpSR[i];
  }

  
  phyDenL ~ normal(mu_phyD, sigma_phyDen);
} 

generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  for (n in 1:N){
    log_lik[n] = normal_lpdf( phyDenL[n] | mu_phyD[n], sigma_phyDen);
  }
}

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Using generated quantities to calculate log likelihood
parts:
Any variables defined in the model block can be used only in the model block.
If you want to use any such variables in the generated quantities then you’ll
have to redefine them.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Using generated quantities to calculate log likelihood
parts:
Hi Chang, 

Variables declared in the model block are only available in the model block. One thing you can do is declare and define the variable in the transformed parameters block (in which case it will be available both in the model and generated quantities blocks), but then that variable will be saved (unlike in the model block). Instead, what I typically do in a case like this is define a function in the functions block that returns the quantity I need and then I use that function in both the model block and generated quantities blocks (instead of copying and pasting the code in both blocks). 

Jonah
